column8: Internal. The algorithm itself is tier A: the prototype subdict.py runs it in the current subset for int keys and gives the same results. Lookups with a native-cost hash: 3.7 vs 3.6 ns at n=1000, 13.8 vs 8.9 ns at 100k, about 40 vs 25 ns at 4M; the large-table gap comes from 8-byte idx slots and the List indirection. PORT HAZARD: with signed ints, p >>= 5 is an arithmetic shift, so a negative hash drives p to -1 and the step becomes i = 5i mod 2^k, which never visits every slot (slot 0 maps to itself), so a lookup can loop forever. In the C, termination depends on the invariant that at most 1/3 of the 2*size idx slots are in use; the loop has no bound.
